hero.headline: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes During Test at Cape Canaveral Launch Pad
hero.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a static fire test at Cape Canaveral's Launch Complex 36 in Florida on Thursday night, destroying the launchpad in a massive fireball visible across the space coast. The explosion occurred at 9pm ET and was powerful enough to shake homes in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach, with an orange sky visible as far south as Fort Pierce, 115 miles away.

The incident poses a significant threat to NASA's lunar ambitions. Just days before the explosion, NASA had selected Blue Origin to conduct the first of three uncrewed lunar missions planned for this year to begin construction of a $20 billion moon base. The New Glenn rocket is the same vehicle Blue Origin intends to use to launch lunar landers for NASA, including the landers that will carry astronauts to the moon's surface under the Artemis program.

Blue Origin confirmed that all employees were safe and unaccounted for following the explosion. Company founder Jeff Bezos described it as "a very rough day" on social media, stating the company would work to identify the root cause and rebuild as needed. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman called spaceflight "unforgiving" and pledged that NASA would work with Blue Origin to investigate the incident and assess impacts to the Artemis and Moon Base programs.

The explosion represents another setback for Blue Origin as it competes with SpaceX for NASA contracts. The company had recently faced grounding by the Federal Aviation Administration after a payload from a New Glenn flight ended up in the wrong orbit last month. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared the rocket to return to flight the previous week.

The incident carries significant implications for NASA's timeline. The space agency had planned to test both Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander and SpaceX's Starship Human Landing System during the Artemis III mission in 2027 to determine which system will transport the Artemis IV crew from the Orion capsule to the lunar surface in 2028. The explosion threatens these schedules.

News of the disaster reverberated through the financial markets. Stock prices for space companies AST SpaceMobile and Rocket Lab declined following reports of the explosion, reflecting investor concerns about the broader commercial space sector and confidence in space operations.

The launchpad remained aflame more than two hours after the initial explosion. Emergency officials reported no threats from fumes or other potential hazards to surrounding areas. The extent of damage to Launch Complex 36 will likely determine when operations can resume at the facility.

cards.headline: Trump delays decision on Iran ceasefire proposal
cards.teaser: President Trump postponed making a final determination on a tentative ceasefire agreement with Iran after meeting with advisers.
cards.body:
President Trump convened a meeting with senior advisers in the Situation Room to make a final decision on an Iran ceasefire proposal, but announced no outcome. U.S. and Iranian officials have confirmed they reached agreement on a deal framework that now requires Trump's approval to proceed.

Vice President Vance indicated the two countries have achieved progress in their negotiations. The agreement remains tentative pending the president's backing.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Drop as U.S. and Iran Near Agreement
cards.teaser: Oil markets declined and stock indexes fluctuated as investors responded to signs that the United States and Iran may reach a deal to extend a cease-fire.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell Friday as markets assessed tentative indications that the United States and Iran are moving closer to an agreement that could extend a cease-fire. Stock markets also showed volatility as investors weighed the potential implications of a pact between the two nations.

The price movements reflected trader expectations that a deal could affect oil supply dynamics in global markets. Iran holds significant oil reserves, and agreements involving the country can influence production and export levels. Financial markets have been monitoring negotiations between U.S. and Iranian officials as they work toward a potential agreement on extending the current cease-fire arrangement.

cards.headline: Nine dead in Longview paper mill chemical tank rupture
cards.body:
Nine people have been confirmed dead following a catastrophic chemical tank rupture at a paper mill in Longview, Washington. Two additional workers remain missing and presumed dead, bringing the expected total death toll to eleven.

The disaster occurred Tuesday morning at the Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co facility. Recovery crews retrieved the remains of six victims by Friday. Authorities have indicated there is no realistic hope of finding additional survivors among those still unaccounted for, and search operations have shifted from rescue to recovery efforts.

The ruptured tank contained approximately 600,000 gallons of white liquor, a highly corrosive chemical mixture primarily composed of sodium hydroxide and sodium sulfide. This substance is used in the kraft paper production process to break down wood fiber. The chemical spill has resulted in environmental contamination, with dead fish discovered in the Columbia River following the rupture.

Recovery operations proceeded carefully due to safety concerns about the structural integrity of the damaged tank. Recovery crews worked in chemical protective equipment, with all recovered victims undergoing decontamination before being transported to the coroner. Recovery officials described the operation as slow, methodical and deliberate, prioritizing both responder safety and dignified treatment of victims.

The Longview fire department stated that approximately 25,000 gallons of the chemical remained in the tank and continued to leak slowly. The spill entered drainage ditches and eventually reached the river. Testing revealed water contamination, and authorities advised the public to avoid ditches and dikes in the area. However, officials reported no threats to air quality or drinking water supplies in Longview.

The sprawling paper mill employs approximately 1,000 workers and produces materials for tissues, printing paper, cups, plates and cartons. The facility is located along the Columbia River in an area with significant timber and chemical industries.

Washington Governor Bob Ferguson called the incident potentially the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington state history. The US Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board announced it was launching a federal investigation into the tank failure.

Safety complaints were filed against Nippon Dynawave in March and May, though state labor authorities said these were unrelated to the current incident. Records show the company has faced three separate health and safety violations since 2021, resulting in a $3,400 fine.

Nippon Dynawave, a subsidiary of Japan-based Nippon Paper Group, stated the company would cooperate fully with the investigation. A company representative said the firm was focused on assisting victims and supporting first responders.

The names of the deceased and missing workers have not been released. The cause of the tank rupture remains under investigation.

cards.headline: Iranian Hard-Liners Push Back Against US Negotiations
cards.teaser: A small faction in Iran has mounted a public campaign to undermine talks with the United States.
cards.body:
Iran's Hard-Liners Try to Derail Potential Deal With the U.S.

A political struggle is unfolding in Iran as hard-liners work to undermine ongoing negotiations with the United States. The opposition faction has mobilized through public rallies, state media appearances, and official statements to voice their resistance to a potential agreement.

Beyond their public campaigns, hard-liners have also pursued private channels to sabotage the talks. These efforts continue as US and Iranian officials advance toward establishing a framework for a deal.

cards.headline: SEC Proposes Repealing Climate Disclosure Rule for Companies
cards.teaser: The Securities and Exchange Commission moved to eliminate a rule requiring companies to report greenhouse gas emissions and climate risks.
cards.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission has proposed repealing a rule requiring publicly traded companies to disclose their greenhouse gas emissions and climate-related financial risks. The disclosure requirement, implemented under the Biden administration and SEC Chair Gary Gensler, aimed to give investors standardized information about how companies manage climate-related risks.

If approved, the repeal would eliminate mandatory emissions reporting and climate risk assessment requirements for companies. The proposal reflects a shift in regulatory approach under the current administration.

cards.headline: SpaceX receives $6.45 billion in Space Force contracts
cards.teaser: The company disclosed that government contracts already accounted for one-fifth of its 2025 revenue in its IPO filing.
cards.body:
SpaceX has received $6.45 billion in contracts from the United States Space Force. The awards come as the aerospace company moves toward going public.

According to SpaceX's IPO filing, government contracts already account for one-fifth of the company's 2025 revenue. These new Space Force contracts expand the company's existing government business as it transitions to publicly traded status.

hero.headline: Russian Drone Strikes Apartment Building in Romania
hero.body:
A Russian drone crashed into an apartment building in Galati, Romania during an overnight attack on Ukraine, injuring two people. The incident marks the first time such a strike has caused civilian casualties on Romanian soil, though drones from the neighboring conflict have previously entered Romanian airspace.

The drone struck the roof of the residential building on Friday, sparking a fire and forcing the evacuation of several residents. Romanian authorities confirmed the drone's origin and immediately convened emergency meetings to discuss the security implications.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte responded swiftly, stating the alliance is "ready to defend every inch" of allied territory. "Russia's reckless behaviour is a danger to us all," Rutte wrote on social media following a call with Romanian President Nicusor Dan.

Romania's Foreign Minister Oana Toiu said the country would communicate the consequences of this incident for diplomatic relations with Russia and would pursue next steps at the European level regarding sanctions. The foreign ministry described the strike as a "grave and irresponsible escalation" and a serious breach of international law. Romania requested that NATO accelerate the transfer of anti-drone capabilities and indicated it would invoke Article 4 of the NATO treaty, which triggers formal discussions about security threats to member states.

Romanian military forces scrambled two F-16 fighter jets and a helicopter in response, while emergency alerts were issued to residents in affected areas.

Vladimir Putin downplayed Russian responsibility, suggesting without evidence that the drone might have been a stray Ukrainian weapon. He said he had only recently learned of the incident and called for the drone wreckage to be handed over to Russia for independent investigation.

The strike represents the latest example of the Ukraine conflict spilling beyond the country's borders. Romanian military officials emphasized that while the strike was not a direct attack from Russia against Romania, Russians should understand that Russia poses a threat to regional security.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the incident demonstrated that Russian aggression threatens all of Europe, not just the Black Sea region. France's Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot condemned the "irresponsible act," while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Russia's "war of aggression has crossed yet another line."

The incident comes as Russia intensifies systematic strikes against Ukraine and as UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres reported that more civilians have been killed in Ukraine's first four months of this year than in comparable periods in previous years. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has pressed the US to provide additional Patriot air defense missiles to counter Russian ballistic missile attacks.

cards.headline: Trump Delays Decision on Iran Cease-Fire Proposal
cards.teaser: The president met with aides about a possible cease-fire extension after suggesting he was ready to decide.
cards.body:
President Trump met with advisers at the White House for two hours to discuss a potential Iran cease-fire extension. A senior administration official confirmed the meeting took place, though Trump delayed announcing a final decision despite earlier suggesting he was ready to act.

U.S. and Iranian officials had previously agreed on a framework for a deal. However, no agreement was announced following the White House meeting.

cards.headline: European Union to Release Billions to Hungary After Electoral Defeat
cards.teaser: The EU is set to release 16 billion euros it had withheld as Hungary enacts reforms.
cards.body:
The European Union will release over €16 billion to Hungary that was frozen during Viktor Orbán's tenure. The decision follows the election of Péter Magyar as prime minister last month, which EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described as bringing "winds of change" to the country.

The breakthrough extends beyond financial matters. Hungarian police have announced they will permit next month's Pride parade in Budapest to proceed, reversing last year's government ban on the event. Magyar called the EU's decision a "historic breakthrough" for Hungary.

cards.headline: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty to Aiding 14 Suicides
cards.teaser: Kenneth Law admitted to charges relating to Canadian victims after selling toxic chemicals online.
cards.body:
Kenneth Law appeared in an Ontario courtroom on Friday to plead guilty to 14 counts of assisting suicide. Prosecutors withdrew 14 murder charges as part of the agreement. Law mailed packets containing lethal chemicals to more than 100 people across dozens of countries, including Canada, the UK, the US, Italy, Australia, and New Zealand.

Families of victims in Britain are calling for additional charges related to 79 deaths there. Sentencing is scheduled for September.

cards.headline: Ghana Passes Bill Criminalizing LGBTQ Identity
cards.teaser: Same-sex acts are now punishable by jail terms under legislation targeting gay, lesbian, and transgender individuals.
cards.body:
Ghana's parliament has passed legislation that criminalizes same-sex acts, subjecting offenders to jail time. The bill also targets individuals who identify as gay, lesbian, or transgender.

The law marks a major change for sexual minorities in the West African country, establishing criminal penalties for both same-sex conduct and gender identity expression.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Boat Strikes Fail to Reduce Cocaine Supply
cards.teaser: Researchers say cocaine remains as available in the US as before military operations began off South America.
cards.body:
Military strikes against boats off the South American coast have not reduced the flow of cocaine into the United States, according to experts. Researchers report that cocaine is as easy to obtain in many parts of the country as it was before the operations began.

The body count has risen as a result of the Trump administration's strikes, but the policy has failed to curb drug trafficking. The assessment challenges the effectiveness of the military approach to interdicting cocaine shipments.

cards.headline: Judge orders Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center
cards.teaser: A federal judge ruled that President Trump's name must be removed from the Kennedy Center memorial.
cards.body:
A federal judge has ordered that Trump's name be removed from the Kennedy Center, the nation's premier performing arts venue in Washington. The ruling also requires the center to remain open and operational.

Trump responded to the court decision by stating he has no interest in the Kennedy Center. He had previously announced plans for a two-year closure to conduct extensive renovations at the facility.

cards.headline: ICE agent charged in Minneapolis shooting arrested in Texas
cards.teaser: An ICE agent wanted in connection with a shooting during an immigration operation in Minneapolis was captured in Texas.
cards.body:
Federal authorities arrested ICE agent Christian Castro in Texas on Friday, 11 days after Minneapolis prosecutors charged him with assault and falsely reporting a crime. Castro had been wanted in connection with the shooting of a Venezuelan man during immigration enforcement activities in Minnesota in January.

Video evidence of the non-fatal shooting emerged, leading to the charges against Castro. The arrest concluded a multistate search for the federal officer.

cards.headline: Airlines warn against customs officer removal from Newark airport
cards.teaser: Airlines and business groups raised concerns about potential travel disruptions if customs officers are pulled from Newark airport.
cards.body:
Airlines and business groups warned of potential chaos if the administration restricts international flights as part of a plan targeting jurisdictions designated as sanctuary cities. The proposal under consideration by officials would involve removing customs officers from Newark airport.

The plan to punish sanctuary jurisdictions by targeting their airports has drawn opposition from the airline industry. Business groups urged the administration not to curb international flights in the dispute over immigration enforcement.

cards.headline: Lead prosecutor withdraws from James Comey case
cards.teaser: The lead federal prosecutor in the case against former FBI Director James Comey stepped aside without providing an explanation.
cards.body:
The lead prosecutor handling the Justice Department's case against James Comey withdrew from the matter. The case involves allegations that Comey posted seashells arranged to read '86 47' in a manner prosecutors claim threatened Trump.

The trial has been moved to October. The prosecutor's departure came without public explanation for the decision to step aside from the case.

cards.headline: Trump postpones call with Taiwan president
cards.teaser: A planned phone call between President Trump and the president of Taiwan has been put on hold.
cards.body:
The Trump administration delayed a scheduled call with Taiwan's president. The postponement comes amid ongoing discussions about U.S. arms sales to Taiwan.

Arms sales to Taiwan remain a point of tension with China. A delayed arms deal to Taiwan reportedly focuses on air defense systems.

cards.headline: Stock Indexes Close at Records as S&P 500 Extends Winning Streak to Nine Weeks
cards.teaser: Major stock indexes reached new closing highs, led by technology companies including Dell, with the S&P 500 posting its ninth consecutive weekly gain.
cards.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all closed at record levels Friday, capping a strong month for U.S. equities. Dell led technology sector gains, which drove much of the broader market advance. The Nasdaq gained 8 percent for the month of May.

The S&P 500 extended its winning streak to nine consecutive weeks. Oil prices fluctuated as investors assessed tentative signs of a potential agreement between the United States and Iran, which supported market optimism. Wall Street closed out May with multiple indexes at all-time highs.

cards.headline: Universal Music Rejects $64 Billion Takeover Offer From Bill Ackman
cards.teaser: Universal Music Group declined a takeover proposal from billionaire investor Bill Ackman's Pershing Square, saying the bid undervalued the company.
cards.body:
Universal Music Group has rejected a $64 billion takeover proposal from Pershing Square, the investment firm controlled by billionaire Bill Ackman. The music company determined that the offer fundamentally undervalued the business.

Pershing Square already holds a stake in Universal Music Group, which manages recording rights for major artists and commands a substantial share of the global music industry. The board's rejection dealt a blow to Ackman's bid to acquire one of the world's largest music companies.

cards.headline: Moringa Supplement Recalled After Salmonella Outbreak Sickens Residents in Washington
cards.teaser: Health authorities linked a salmonella outbreak affecting people in eastern and western Washington to moringa capsules sold through Amazon, Walmart, and Target.
cards.body:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the Food and Drug Administration announced a recall of moringa supplement capsules after linking them to a multistate salmonella outbreak. Residents in both eastern and western Washington were among those sickened by the contaminated products.

The recalled supplements were sold through major retailers including Amazon, TikTok Shop, Walmart, and Target. The FDA issued the recall announcement after confirming the connection between the moringa capsules and reported salmonella cases. Consumers who purchased the affected supplements are being advised to stop using them and dispose of them or return them to retailers.

cards.teaser: A maintenance train fire near Penn Station during rush hour injured five people and suspended service for Am

hero.headline: Proposed US funding rules would allow grant cancellations at any time
hero.body:
The United States government has proposed new rules for research funding that would allow federal agencies to cancel grants at any time. The proposed changes would also make peer review optional in the grant approval process.

Under the new rules, political staff would screen grant applications for forbidden topics. The changes represent a shift in how federal research funding operates, moving away from the traditional peer review system that has been standard practice for evaluating scientific merit.

The proposal eliminates the requirement for independent expert review before grants are awarded. Instead, political appointees would have authority to evaluate applications based on topic restrictions. The rules would also give agencies discretion to terminate funding agreements without the constraints that currently govern grant relationships.

Federal research grants currently operate under agreements that protect ongoing work from arbitrary cancellation. The proposed rules would remove those protections, allowing agencies to end funding at their discretion regardless of a project's status or the terms under which it was originally awarded.

The peer review process has traditionally served as a buffer between political considerations and scientific evaluation. Experts in relevant fields assess grant applications based on methodology, feasibility, and potential contribution to knowledge. The proposed optional status for this review would allow grants to be approved or denied without that independent assessment.

The topic screening provision directs political staff to identify and potentially reject proposals that address subjects deemed forbidden, though the proposal does not specify which topics would fall into that category. This screening would occur before scientific review, if such review takes place at all.

Researchers rely on federal grants as a primary funding source for work across scientific disciplines. The ability to cancel grants at any time could affect ongoing projects that have already allocated resources and hired personnel based on multi-year funding commitments. The rules would apply to new grants issued after the regulations take effect.

cards.headline: Kenyan court blocks US plan to send Ebola-exposed Americans to Kenya
cards.teaser: The United States has previously built specialized facilities for treating Americans exposed to infectious diseases.
cards.body:
A Kenyan court has blocked a Trump administration plan to construct a quarantine and treatment center in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola during an outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The ruling prevents the transfer of affected individuals to the facility.

The White House had confirmed it was building the center in Kenya as an alternative to bringing exposed Americans back to the United States for isolation and treatment. Some experts have criticized this approach, arguing that preventing Americans from returning home could hinder treatment efforts.

cards.headline: Botnet using 17 million devices dismantled
cards.teaser: The network was linked to a Russia-based residential proxy operation.
cards.body:
A botnet comprising more than 17 million devices has been taken down. The network of compromised computers and connected devices was operating on a scale that made it one of the larger known botnets.

The botnet was tied to a residential proxy network based in Russia. Residential proxy networks route internet traffic through home devices, often without the knowledge of the device owners, to mask the true origin of online activity.

cards.headline: Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm tease new N1X laptop processors
cards.teaser: The companies coordinated social media posts ahead of an industry event, with Lenovo confirming it is developing laptops using the chips.
cards.body:
Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm are teasing the upcoming announcement of Nvidia's N1X laptop processors ahead of Computex this weekend. The Windows and Nvidia GeForce accounts on X both posted "A new era of PC," followed by a similar message from Arm, signaling a coordinated reveal.

Microsoft's Surface chief Pavan Davuluri has also teased new hardware coming for developers, sharing a mysterious image suggesting a curved display design. The announcements hint at upcoming innovations for Nvidia's Arm-based laptop chips and potentially new Surface devices.

cards.headline: Texas measles outbreak analysis shows one in five cases hospitalized
cards.teaser: Most hospitalized patients developed complications from the virus.
cards.body:
Original card text retained

An analysis of a measles outbreak in Texas found that approximately one in five cases required hospitalization. Most of the hospitalized patients developed complications from the infection.

The study provides data on the severity of measles cases in the outbreak. Measles is a highly contagious viral disease that can lead to serious health problems, and the Texas outbreak demonstrated the rate at which infected individuals required hospital care and experienced medical complications beyond the initial infection.

---

Reason: The additional source material provided does not contain information about the Texas measles outbreak. The sources reference a European dump cleanup project and a baseball fan's catches—neither of which relates to the measles story. Therefore, the original card text is returned unchanged.

cards.headline: Coders increasingly refuse to work without AI assistance
cards.teaser: Researchers warn that while AI helps programmers write code faster, it may not be producing better quality code.
cards.body:
Software developers are becoming reluctant to work without AI coding tools, reflecting how quickly these systems have become integrated into their workflows. The technology enables programmers to write code faster by automating generation and completion tasks.

However, researchers caution that speed improvements may come at a cost. While AI-assisted coding accelerates production, studies suggest it doesn't necessarily improve code quality. This disconnect could create hidden problems that surface later during software maintenance and updates.

hero.headline: Teenager Joao Fonseca upsets Novak Djokovic at French Open
hero.body:
Nineteen-year-old Brazilian Joao Fonseca defeated Novak Djokovic in five sets during the third round of the French Open. The upset ensures there will be a new men's Grand Slam champion at Roland Garros this year.

Djokovic, 39, lost on the red clay courts in Paris to the teenage competitor. The defeat represents a major opportunity lost for the veteran player in his pursuit of a 25th Grand Slam title.

Fonseca's victory marks a significant moment in his young career. The win over one of tennis's most decorated players demonstrates the Brazilian's arrival among the sport's top competitors.

The match took place during a tournament that has seen multiple favorites eliminated. Djokovic's loss continues a pattern of upsets at this year's French Open.

The result means the men's singles championship will go to someone who has never won a Grand Slam tournament before. Djokovic had been seeking to add to his record of major titles.

Fonseca executed a five-set victory against the experienced champion. The young player's performance showed his ability to compete at the highest level of professional tennis.

Djokovic's elimination removes one of the tournament favorites from contention. The 39-year-old had entered the French Open as one of the players expected to compete for the title.

The upset victory propels Fonseca into the next round of the tournament. His win over Djokovic represents one of the biggest results of the French Open so far.

The match showcased the generational shift taking place in men's tennis. Fonseca, at 19, defeated a player twice his age who has dominated the sport for nearly two decades.

Djokovic's loss on the Paris clay courts ends his bid for another French Open title this year. The defeat came earlier in the tournament than many tennis observers had anticipated.

cards.headline: Washington Nationals fire executive over hidden-camera video comments
cards.teaser: The team dismissed an official after a video showed him discussing the team's social media practices regarding a conservative player.
cards.body:
The Washington Nationals terminated an executive after a hidden-camera video captured comments about the team's social media strategy regarding a conservative player. According to the recording, the executive stated the organization deliberately avoided featuring this player in its social media content.

The video also showed the executive discussing the team's treatment of a Catholic pitcher. Following the release of the recording, the Nationals' baseball operations division came under potential scrutiny from the Department of Justice regarding allegations of religious discrimination based on statements made in the video.

cards.headline: Pentagon recruits troops for White House UFC fights with weight requirements
cards.teaser: Internal memos show the Defense Department is selecting service members to attend UFC events at the White House based on fitness standards.
cards.body:
The Pentagon has begun recruiting troops to watch UFC fights at the White House, according to internal memos. Service members must meet weight standards to receive free tickets to the events.

The UFC released renderings for the White House fight and a Freedom250 Fan Fest. Podcast host Joe Rogan raised concerns about safety at the planned White House UFC event. No heavyweight fighters will be permitted to attend under the fitness criteria established for troops.

cards.headline: Giants players Abdul Carter and Jaxson Dart address Trump rally dispute
cards.teaser: Two New York Giants players publicly discussed their disagreement after quarterback Jaxson Dart introduced President Trump at a political rally.
cards.body:
Giants defensive end Abdul Carter publicly disagreed with quarterback Jaxson Dart's decision to introduce President Donald Trump at a rally. Carter felt compelled to make his opposition to Trump known in response to his teammate's appearance at the political event.

The two players subsequently discussed their differences and expressed a unified front. The disagreement drew attention from NFL media outlets covering how the teammates navigated their differing political views.

cards.headline: MLB suspends Brewers pitcher Abner Uribe one game for celebration
cards.teaser: The league disciplined the reliever for making a crotch-chopping gesture during a game against the Cardinals.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball suspended Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Abner Uribe for one game following a crotch-chop celebration during the team's win over the St. Louis Cardinals. The league also issued an undisclosed fine for what it deemed an unacceptable gesture.

Uribe is appealing the suspension. The celebration, which recalled a gesture associated with professional wrestling's D-Generation X, was documented on video during the game.

cards.headline: Sacramento launches bid for MLB expansion team
cards.teaser: An investor group in California's capital city announced efforts to bring Major League Baseball to Sacramento.
cards.body:
A Sacramento-based investment group has launched a formal effort to bring Major League Baseball to the city as part of MLB's expansion consideration process. The bid has generated enthusiasm among local fans who have expressed their support for professional baseball in Sacramento.

Sacramento is competing against other cities for expansion franchises, including Vancouver and teams in Tampa that are exploring stadium options. The investor group behind the Sacramento bid includes several prominent local figures committed to the effort.

cards.headline: NCAA baseball tournament begins with regional play
cards.teaser: The 2026 Men's College World Series bracket was released as teams prepare for regional competition.
cards.body:
The NCAA announced the bracket and schedule for the 2026 baseball tournament. Regional play began with matchups across the country as teams compete for spots in the College World Series.

Analysts previewed key storylines including UCLA's championship prospects and whether the Southeastern Conference will claim another title. Top players to watch and predictions for the regionals were released by major sports networks covering college baseball.

hero.headline: Marcia Lucas, Oscar-Winning Star Wars Editor, Dies at 80
hero.body:
Marcia Lucas, the Oscar-winning film editor who shaped Star Wars and several influential films of the 1970s, died Wednesday in Rancho Mirage, California. She was 80. The family's attorney confirmed she died of cancer.

Lucas won an Academy Award for editing Star Wars, directed by her former husband George Lucas. Her work on the film helped define modern science fiction cinema and influenced a generation of filmmakers.

Beyond Star Wars, Lucas edited American Graffiti and contributed to other films that defined 1970s cinema. Her editing skills were instrumental in shaping the narrative structure and pacing of these landmark productions.

The family attorney described her as a brilliant storyteller and a trailblazer in the film industry. Lucas was known for her precise sense of timing and ability to craft compelling narratives through editing choices that enhanced both character development and dramatic tension.

Lucas began her career in the film industry during an era when few women held prominent technical roles in Hollywood. Her success as an editor helped open doors for future generations of women working in post-production.

Her editing work on Star Wars proved particularly influential. The film's groundbreaking use of cross-cutting during the climactic battle sequence and its carefully paced reveal of key story elements demonstrated her mastery of the craft.

After her divorce from George Lucas, Marcia stepped back from high-profile film work but remained respected within the industry for her contributions to cinema. Her work on American Graffiti, which earned critical acclaim and commercial success, showcased her range beyond science fiction.

Lucas is survived by her family in California. Memorial arrangements have not been announced. The film industry has lost one of its pioneering editors whose work continues to influence filmmakers and editors today.

cards.headline: Over Half of Great American State Fair Performers Drop Out
cards.teaser: More than half of scheduled performers have withdrawn from a Trump-backed concert planned for America's 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
Multiple artists have withdrawn from the US Freedom 250 concert, a Trump-backed event planned as part of America's 250th anniversary celebrations. More than half of the originally scheduled performers have dropped out of the Great American State Fair.

The departures follow disputes over politics and reported threats. The concert is part of a parallel celebration to the official America250 commemoration, creating what has been described as two separate party planners for the nation's birthday.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remainder of 2026 Tour
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old singer announced he is canceling all remaining concert dates for 2026 due to health issues.
cards.body:
The 92-year-old performer announced Friday that he is canceling his remaining concert dates for 2026 to focus on his health. Valli, who has maintained an active touring schedule throughout his career, shared the news via social media and expressed his apologies to ticket holders.

The legendary singer did not elaborate on the specific nature of his health concerns or discuss potential future touring plans.

cards.headline: A24's Backrooms Earns Over $10 Million in Previews
cards.teaser: The horror film from 20-year-old director Kane Parsons has already earned more than $10 million before its nationwide release.
cards.body:
Kane Parsons' directorial debut "Backrooms" has already grossed over $10 million during its preview screenings. The A24 horror film is now in wide theatrical release.

The movie features an ensemble cast including Chiwetel Ejiofor, Renate Reinsve, and Mark Duplass. Adapted from the original Backrooms YouTube series, the film marks a significant box office achievement for the 20-year-old filmmaker.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Councilwoman Urges Governor Candidates to Support Film Tax Credits
cards.teaser: Nithya Raman appeared with entertainment figures to call for uncapped tax incentives for film and TV production in California.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Councilwoman Nithya Raman urged candidates for governor to support uncapped tax incentives for film and TV production. Raman, who is running for mayor, appeared outside Radford Studios with entertainment industry figures who support her campaign.

Producers Mike Schur, Cord Jefferson, and Kay Cannon joined Raman at the event. The Tuesday election is approaching, and Raman emphasized the importance of keeping Hollywood production in California through enhanced tax credit programs.

cards.headline: Kanye West Cleared to Perform in Netherlands
cards.teaser: Dutch officials ruled that insufficient evidence exists to ban the rapper from entering the country for a birthday performance.
cards.body:
Officials in the Netherlands have cleared Kanye West to perform in the country on his birthday. The ruling came after authorities reviewed whether to ban the rapper from entering the country.

Dutch officials determined that insufficient evidence had been found to justify preventing West from performing. The decision allows the concert to proceed as scheduled on the rapper's birthday.

cards.headline: 13 Reasons Why Stars Reunite at Filipino Forces Event
cards.teaser: Ross Butler and Timothy Granaderos attended the fourth annual Filipino Forces dinner in Hollywood.
cards.body:
Ross Butler and Timothy Granaderos, who starred together in 13 Reasons Why, reunited at the fourth annual Filipino Forces event in Hollywood. The dinner brought together influential Filipinos from fashion, entertainment, and technology.

Other attendees included Chief of War actor Brandon Finn, Januel Mercado who wrote and directed Dreamworks Animation's Forgotten Island, and The Pitt star Kristin Villanueva. The event highlighted Filipino representation across multiple industries.

hero.headline: Judge orders Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center
hero.body:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C. ordered President Trump to remove his name from the Kennedy Center and halted planned renovations at the performing arts venue.

District Judge issued the ruling on Friday, giving the president two weeks to remove his name from the building and surrounding signage. The 94-page order also stopped the center's scheduled closure, which was set to begin later this year for a two-year renovation project.

The judge wrote that it was crystal clear the arts complex was named for President John F. Kennedy. The ruling found that the Kennedy Center's board overstepped its statutory authority by unilaterally deciding to add Trump's name and proceed with the renovation plans.

The decision blocks Trump's effort to renovate the facility, which serves as the national cultural center. The board had planned to close the venue to the public while construction took place.

The ruling also prevents the center from winding down its programming, meaning performances and events will continue as scheduled. The judge determined that closing the facility for renovations would exceed the board's legal powers under its governing statute.

Trump has not yet commented on the order. The Kennedy Center board must now decide whether to appeal the decision or comply with the two-week deadline to remove all references to the president's name from the property.

The case represents a legal setback for Trump's plans to reshape one of Washington's most prominent cultural institutions. The Kennedy Center, located along the Potomac River, hosts theater, opera, ballet, and symphony performances throughout the year.

The facility's status as a presidential memorial has been central to the legal dispute. Congress created the center as a living memorial to President Kennedy, and the judge's ruling reinforces that original designation.

cards.headline: Pentagon awards Dell $9.7 billion contract amid Trump stock concerns
cards.teaser: The Department of Defense signed a five-year deal with Dell after President Trump bought company stock and promoted its products.
cards.body:
I appreciate you sharing these additional sources, but they don't appear to contain details about the Dell Pentagon contract story. The Guardian piece covers Utah's voter roll audit, and The Verge article discusses SpaceX's separate $4.16 billion contract for satellite development.

Since the additional source material doesn't provide new confirmed facts about the Dell contract, I'm returning the original card text unchanged:

The Pentagon awarded Dell a $9.7 billion contract for Microsoft software and cloud services, raising questions about potential conflicts of interest involving President Trump.

The Department of Defense announced the five-year agreement on Wednesday as part of an effort to consolidate its technology services. The deal came after Trump publicly promoted Dell products and purchased significant amounts of the company's stock.

cards.headline: Judge allows Trump's $10 billion IRS lawsuit to proceed
cards.teaser: A federal judge in Florida reopened President Trump's case against the IRS after intervenors challenged a settlement agreement.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Florida agreed to reopen President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS. The decision allows the case to proceed after intervenors objected to a proposed settlement between Trump and the Department of Justice.

The two parties had sought to voluntarily dismiss the case in exchange for establishing an "anti-weaponization" fund. The judge determined that those challenging the settlement had sufficient grounds to continue the legal action and require further scrutiny of the agreement.

cards.headline: Bessent backs putting Trump on proposed $250 bill
cards.teaser: The Treasury secretary endorsed a commemorative currency bill featuring President Trump during an interview at the Reagan Library.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent endorsed a $250 bill featuring President Trump's portrait, saying it would commemorate the nation's 250th anniversary of independence. Speaking at a White House news conference, Bessent said the Treasury has already begun preparing for the potential new currency.

The proposal would require Congress to change federal law, which currently prohibits living people from appearing on US currency. While the White House is pushing for approval, Democrats have vowed to block the measure.

cards.headline: Trump endorses Evette over Rep. Mace in South Carolina governor race
cards.teaser: President Trump backed Lieutenant Governor Pam Evette instead of Rep. Nancy Mace for the South Carolina gubernatorial contest.
cards.body:
Trump endorsed Lt. Gov. Pam Evette in the South Carolina gubernatorial race on Friday, backing her over Rep. Nancy Mace's campaign for governor. The endorsement marks a notable split between Trump and Mace.

In his endorsement, Trump praised Evette as a strong candidate in the Republican primary contest.

cards.headline: Talarico leads Paxton by three points in Texas governor poll
cards.teaser: State Rep. James Talarico holds a narrow advantage over Attorney General Ken Paxton in a new survey of likely voters.
cards.body:
Democratic state Rep. James Talarico led Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton by three percentage points in a Texas governor race poll released Friday.

The Texas Public Opinion Research survey showed 47 percent of likely general election voters backed Talarico, while 44 percent supported Paxton. The poll was conducted after the primary runoff elections in the state.

cards.headline: New Jersey detention facility tests DHS Secretary Mullin
cards.teaser: Protests and a reported hunger strike at Delaney Hall present the first major challenge for Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin.
cards.body:
A private detention center in New Jersey has become a flashpoint in disputes over Trump administration immigration policies, marking the first major test for Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. Protests and a reported hunger strike at the Delaney Hall Facility in Newark have drawn attention to claims of inhumane conditions and inadequate medical care.

New Jersey officials announced state police will take over policing functions from federal immigration officers at the facility. Governor Mikie Sherrill and Attorney General Jennifer Davenport said state police will establish a "peaceful protected zone" for demonstrators as part of their public safety operations at the site.
